import json

with open('crash/09793.json') as f:
    test = json.load(f)

print(list(test.keys()))
print(test['vehicle'])
print(test['test'])

for key, ch in test['channels'].items():
    print(f"{key:12} {ch['comment']:34} "
          f"{ch['dimension']:13} {ch['unit']:8} {ch['status']}")

print({(ch['n'], ch['dt'], ch['t0']) for ch in test['channels'].values()})

for key, ch in test['channels'].items():
    print(f"{key:12} min {min(ch['y']):10.1f}   max {max(ch['y']):8.1f}   {ch['unit']}")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

for key, ch in test['channels'].items():
    t_ms = [1000 * (ch['t0'] + i * ch['dt']) for i in range(ch['n'])]
    y, unit, dim = ch['y'], ch['unit'], ch['dimension']
    if key == 'chest_d':   # header says m and 'Meters'; values are micrometers
        y, unit, dim = [v / 1000 for v in y], 'mm', 'Displacement'
    plt.figure()
    plt.plot(t_ms, y)
    plt.xlabel('time from impact (ms)')
    plt.ylabel(dim + ' (' + unit + ')')
    plt.title(ch['comment'] + '  [' + ch['code'] + ']')
    plt.show()
